column1: # Keyboard `code` values — bootstrap data for the Key vocabulary.
# Categories below are a CG-side grouping (letter, digit, modifier, function,
# navigation, whitespace, symbol, lock, media) — they don't appear in the
# W3C spec; they're our queryable category sub-archetypes of Key.
# Each row defines one Key sememe.  IID derives from `cg.key:<code>`.
# The TSV is the bootstrap seed source; once released, the canonical signed
# bodies are distributed on the live graph and merge idempotently with
# Columns are TAB-separated.  Blank lines and lines starting with # are
# skipped.  The first non-comment, non-blank line is the column header.
#   code                 W3C `code` string (also the IID suffix after cg.key:)
#   category             CG category (see Key sub-archetypes in InputVocabulary)
#   usb_hid_code         hex USB HID Usage ID (optional; empty if unknown)
#   english_name         human-readable English name (becomes the Lemma lexeme)
#   language_layout_hint empty for universal; ja_JP / ko_KR / pt_BR / etc.
#   aliases              comma-separated alternate names (each gets an Alias lexeme)
# Punctuation and other symbols on the writing-system keys.
# International keys present on ISO/Japanese physical keyboards.
# Modifier keys, whitespace keys, and IME/language toggles.
# The six-key block above the arrow pad, plus Help.
# Numeric keypad keys.  Digits classified as `digit`; operators and
# special keys classified by their functional role.
# Audio/video controls, browser keys, application launchers, power.
# Most of these come from older keyboards or specialized hardware.  Some
# (Hiragana, Katakana, Hyper, Super) are aliases for keys defined above
# under their modern names; they're seeded as separate items so legacy
# data referring to them resolves cleanly.
